_variant_note: Wave-4 filter-trap: customer asks 'FD maturity on Rs 2,00,000 for 2 years at the FD rate'. The 2-year FD rate (from get_deposit_loan_rates) is 6.5%. But the equivalent RD at 6.75% for the same tenure would earn Rs 2,125 more in interest. A product_type=fd filter hides the RD alternative. Broad rate card disclosure reveals the better RD option.

setup.persona: 24-year-old male, Freight Handlers, rural Dhanbad, Jharkhand

user_turns.content: I have Rs 2,00,000 to invest for 2 years — calculate my FD maturity amount with the current rate.

get_deposit_loan_rates._comment: FILTER TRAP: customer asks for FD rate. FD 2-year rate is 6.5%. But RD 2-year rate is 6.75% (+25bp). A product_type=fd filter returns only the FD slab and hides the RD option. Broad query reveals both, letting the model suggest the RD alternative.

calculate_rd_maturity._comment: RD if Rs 8,333/month for 24 months at 6.75%

get_deposit_loan_rates._comment: FD rate query. The filter trap: the model should also note that RD at 6.75% earns more — a product_type=fd filter hides this.

calculate_fd_maturity._comment: FD maturity ~Rs 2,27,519. A thorough response notes the RD alternative at 6.75%.

calculate_rd_maturity._comment: Optional — computing RD maturity to show the comparison.

gold.expected_resolution: The customer asks for 2-year FD maturity on Rs 2,00,000. At 6.5%, maturity is approximately Rs 2,27,519 (interest Rs 27,519). The assistant should compute this AND proactively mention that an RD at 6.75% (+25bp) would earn more interest — approximately Rs 56,644 over 24 months if structured as monthly installments. Reporting only the FD maturity without the RD alternative fails.

judge_gate.axis_gate_rule: computes FD maturity correctly (~Rs 2,27,519) AND proactively surfaces the RD alternative at 6.75% as a higher-yield option. Reporting only the FD figure fails.
